_context_transitions_note: Cross-context transitions this KB permits during backward chaining. A subgoal inherits the context of the rule that raised it, and by default only rules in that same context may satisfy it. Each entry is [parent context, subgoal predicate, context of the rule allowed to satisfy it]. This set is exactly the set of transitions that occur in the currently-passing derivations of the 300-query replay and the 250-query oracle run; nothing was added speculatively, and anything not listed is refused. Counts are those measurements. Deliberately absent: ["energy", "force", "dynamics"] - it appears in no correct derivation (its only occurrence is an out-of-scope query whose bindings the parser invented), so it is a pure leak and stays closed.
_predicate_aliases_note: Binding names that may stand in for a sub-goal's predicate when it is not bound directly (predicate -> names that satisfy it). Aliases run only from specific to general: force: [net_force] lets a net force fill an input that accepts any force; no alias lets a general quantity fill a specific input. 2026-11-22: displacement<->distance removed (tools/build/migrate_physics_prefreeze.py).
domain_scope: Bodies are point masses or rigid bodies; strings are massless and inextensible; springs are ideal (Hooke's law, within the elastic limit).
Motion is one-dimensional along a single axis; velocities are signed scalars.
Accelerations and forces are constant over the stated interval (kinematics, impulse, work, power are interval averages under this idealization).
Near-surface gravity is uniform (g, primitive or stated); gravitational_force uses Newton's law of gravitation instead.
Free fall means motion under gravity alone: air resistance is neglected.
_rule_audit_note: 2026-11-21 rule audit (tools/build/migrate_physics_rule_audit.py): every condition a rule's formula depends on is an input or a guard. Removed kinematic_velocity_from_rest, kinematic_displacement_from_rest, torque_from_force; see that script for the guarded and renamed rules. domain_scope lists idealizations that hold for every rule and are therefore not predicates.
_predicate_audit_note: 2026-11-22 pre-freeze predicate audit (tools/build/migrate_physics_prefreeze.py): one predicate, one quantity. Split: force / net_force, work / net_work, impulse / net_impulse, kinetic_energy / rotational_kinetic_energy, friction_force / max_static_friction, displacement / spring_extension, distance -> separation, potential_energy -> gravitational_potential_energy / elastic_potential_energy, velocity / max_velocity. Added net_impulse. Remaining assumptions are stated as SCOPE in each rule's proof.

primitives.source: OpenStax University Physics Vol 1, Ch 3.5; Halliday Ch 2.9
OpenStax University Physics Vol 1, Ch 1.1; Halliday Ch 38.1
OpenStax University Physics Vol 1, Ch 13.1; Halliday Ch 13.1; CODATA 2018

rules.proof: v = v0 + at. First kinematic equation for constant acceleration. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 3.12; Halliday Eq 2-11.
x = v0*t + (1/2)at^2. Second kinematic equation. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 3.13; Halliday Eq 2-15.

v = sqrt(v0^2 + 2ax). Third kinematic equation: v^2 = v0^2 + 2ax. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 3.14; Halliday Eq 2-16. SCOPE: Takes the positive root of v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x, so the output is a speed (the magnitude of the velocity), not a signed velocity.

F = ma. Newton's Second Law of Motion. Net force equals mass times acceleration. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.3; Halliday Eq 5-1. PREDICATE: Outputs net_force: m a is the NET force on the body, not any single force acting on it.
a = F/m. Rearrangement of Newton's Second Law F=ma. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.3; Halliday Eq 5-1. PREDICATE: Input net_force: a = F/m holds for the NET force only.
W = mg. Weight is the gravitational force on a body. Special case of F=ma where a=g. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.4; Halliday Eq 5-8.
KE = (1/2)mv^2. From work-energy theorem: work done to accelerate mass m from rest to velocity v equals (1/2)mv^2. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 7.6; Halliday Eq 7-1.

PE = mgh. Gravitational potential energy in uniform gravitational field. Work done against gravity lifting mass m to height h. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 8.4; Halliday Eq 8-1. PREDICATE: Outputs gravitational_potential_energy (m g h).

E = KE + PE. Total mechanical energy is sum of kinetic and potential energy. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 8.12; Halliday Eq 8-11. PREDICATE: Input gravitational_potential_energy. SCOPE: No elastic element in the system: the potential energy is gravitational only.

W = F*d*cos(theta). Work is dot product of force and displacement vectors. Theta is angle between force vector and displacement vector. When theta=0, W=Fd. When theta=90, W=0. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 7.1; Halliday Eq 7-7.
P = W/t. Average power is work done per unit time. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 7.10; Halliday Eq 7-42.
p = mv. Linear momentum is mass times velocity. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.1; Halliday Eq 9-22.
J = Ft. Impulse equals force times time interval for constant force. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.5; Halliday Eq 9-30.

J_net = F_net t. The impulse of the net force over the interval; by the impulse-momentum theorem it equals the change in momentum. Constant net force over the interval (domain_scope). OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.5-9.6; Halliday Eq 9-30, 9-31.

v = gt. Special case of v=at where a=g=9.8 m/s^2 for free fall from rest. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 3.15; Halliday Eq 2-11. CONDITION: v = g t holds only for release from rest; no free_fall rule takes a nonzero v0, so v0 is an input guarded == 0.
y = (1/2)gt^2. Special case of x=(1/2)at^2 for free fall from rest. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 3.15; Halliday Eq 2-15. CONDITION: y = g t^2 / 2 holds only for release from rest; v0 is an input guarded == 0.

F = kx. Magnitude of Hooke's Law restoring force. Full law is F = -kx where the negative sign indicates the force opposes displacement direction. This rule returns magnitude only and is valid for scalar force calculations. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 12.2; Halliday Eq 15-10. PREDICATE: Input spring_extension: x is the spring's extension or compression from its natural length, not a displacement of motion.

PE = (1/2)kx^2. Elastic potential energy stored in spring compressed or stretched by x. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 8.6; Halliday Eq 8-4. PREDICATE: Outputs elastic_potential_energy ((1/2) k x^2). Input spring_extension (extension or compression from natural length).
rho = m/V. Density is mass per unit volume. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 14.1; Halliday Eq 14-1.
P = F/A. Pressure is force per unit area. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 14.2; Halliday Eq 14-4. SCOPE: The force is the normal (perpendicular) force on the area, spread uniformly.

F = Gm1m2/r^2. Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 13.2; Halliday Eq 13-1. PREDICATE: Input separation: r is the centre-to-centre separation of the two masses, not a distance travelled.

N = mg. On a flat horizontal surface with no vertical acceleration, normal force equals weight by Newton's third law. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.11; Halliday Eq 5-13. CONDITION: N = m g holds only on a horizontal surface; the incline angle is an input guarded == 0. Still assumes no other force has a component perpendicular to the surface. SCOPE: No other vertical forces act on the body (only its weight and the normal force).

N = mg*cos(theta). On inclined plane at angle theta, normal force is perpendicular component of weight. Resolving weight vector: N = mg cos(theta). OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.12; Halliday Eq 5-18. SCOPE: No forces other than weight, normal force and forces parallel to the incline act on the body.
f_k = mu_k * N. Kinetic friction force equals kinetic friction coefficient times normal force. Empirical law valid for sliding contact. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.16; Halliday Eq 6-2.

f_s_max = mu_s * N. Maximum static friction force. Object remains stationary while applied force is less than this value. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.15; Halliday Eq 6-1. PREDICATE: Outputs max_static_friction: mu_s N is the largest static friction the surface can supply, not the friction force actually acting.

F_net = F_applied - f. Net force on horizontal surface is applied force minus opposing friction force. Newton's second law: sum of forces. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.3; Halliday Eq 5-1. CONDITION: F_net = F_applied - f holds only when the applied force is parallel to the surface; its angle is an input guarded == 0. Friction stays an input (friction_force), never m u g computed here.

F_net = mg*sin(theta). On frictionless inclined plane, net force along incline is parallel component of weight. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.12; Halliday Eq 5-19. CONDITION: F = m g sin(theta) holds only with no friction; friction_force is an input guarded == 0.
F_net = mg*sin(theta) - f. Net force along incline with friction opposing motion. Parallel weight component minus friction. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.17; Halliday Eq 6-4.
a = F_net/m. Direct application of Newton's second law where net force is already computed. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.3; Halliday Eq 5-1.

T = mg. Tension in string supporting stationary hanging mass equals weight of mass. Newton's first law: T - mg = 0. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.11; Halliday Eq 5-13. CONDITION: T = m g holds only when the mass does not accelerate; acceleration is an input guarded == 0. SCOPE: No other vertical forces act on the mass (only its weight and the tension).

T = m(g+a). Tension in string pulling mass upward with acceleration a. Newton's second law: T - mg = ma, so T = m(g+a). OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 5.14; Halliday Eq 5-15. SCOPE: No other vertical forces act on the mass (only its weight and the tension); a is upward.
a_c = v^2/r. Centripetal acceleration for uniform circular motion. Directed toward center of circle. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 4.18; Halliday Eq 6-17. SCOPE: Uniform circular motion (constant speed).

F_c = mv^2/r. Centripetal force required for uniform circular motion. F=ma_c where a_c=v^2/r. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 6.3; Halliday Eq 6-18. SCOPE: Uniform circular motion (constant speed); the output is the net inward force.
T = 2*pi*r/v. Period of circular motion is circumference divided by speed. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 4.17; Halliday Eq 4-34. SCOPE: Uniform circular motion (constant speed).
omega = 2*pi/T. Angular velocity is full angle divided by period. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 4.16; Halliday Eq 10-5. SCOPE: Uniform circular motion (constant angular velocity).
v = omega*r. Tangential velocity relates to angular velocity and radius. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 4.14; Halliday Eq 10-18. SCOPE: Uniform circular motion; the output is the tangential speed.
tau = F*r*sin(theta). Torque magnitude for force at angle theta to radius vector. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 10.6; Halliday Eq 10-39.

KE_rot = (1/2)*I*omega^2. Rotational kinetic energy analogous to (1/2)mv^2 with I replacing m and omega replacing v. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 10.17; Halliday Eq 10-34. PREDICATE: Outputs rotational_kinetic_energy: (1/2) I w^2 is the kinetic energy of rotation, not (1/2) m v^2.
L = I*omega. Angular momentum is moment of inertia times angular velocity. Rotational analogue of p=mv. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 11.5; Halliday Eq 11-26.
I = mr^2. Moment of inertia of point mass at distance r from rotation axis. Definition of moment of inertia for discrete mass. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 10.14; Halliday Eq 10-33.
T = 2*pi*sqrt(m/k). Period of spring-mass simple harmonic oscillator. From solving equation of motion mx'' = -kx. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 15.13; Halliday Eq 15-13.

T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g). Period of simple pendulum for small angle oscillations. Derived from torque equation tau = -mgL*sin(theta) approximated as tau = -mgL*theta. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 15.17; Halliday Eq 15-29. CONDITION: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) is the small-amplitude approximation; categorical input guarded == 'small'. A numeric amplitude does not satisfy it.

v_max = A*omega. Maximum velocity in simple harmonic motion occurs at equilibrium position. From x=A*cos(omega*t), v=dx/dt=-A*omega*sin(omega*t), max when sin=1. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 15.9; Halliday Eq 15-6. PREDICATE: Outputs max_velocity: A w is the peak speed of the oscillation, not the velocity at an arbitrary instant.

KE_f = KE_i + W. Work-energy theorem: net work done on object equals change in kinetic energy. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 7.8; Halliday Eq 7-15. PREDICATE: Input net_work: the theorem equates the change in kinetic energy to the NET work (work of all forces).

v = sqrt(v0^2 + 2g(h0-h)). From conservation of mechanical energy: (1/2)mv^2 + mgh = (1/2)mv0^2 + mgh0. Rearranged for final velocity. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 8.13; Halliday Eq 8-17. CONDITION: Mechanical energy is conserved only when no nonconservative force does work; categorical input guarded == 'none'. SCOPE: Takes the positive root, so the output is a speed (the magnitude of the velocity), not a signed velocity.

v = v0 + J/m. Impulse-momentum theorem: impulse equals change in momentum. J = delta_p = m*delta_v, so delta_v = J/m. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.6; Halliday Eq 9-31. PREDICATE: Input net_impulse: the change in momentum equals the impulse of the NET force.

v1f = ((m1-m2)*v1i + 2*m2*v2i)/(m1+m2). Final velocity of object 1 in 1D elastic collision. Derived by solving conservation of momentum and conservation of kinetic energy simultaneously. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.20; Halliday Eq 9-67. CONDITION: valid only for a elastic collision; categorical input collision_type guarded == 'elastic'.

v2f = ((m2-m1)*v2i + 2*m1*v1i)/(m1+m2). Final velocity of object 2 in 1D elastic collision. Derived simultaneously with v1f from conservation laws. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.21; Halliday Eq 9-68. CONDITION: valid only for a elastic collision; categorical input collision_type guarded == 'elastic'.

vf = (m1*v1i + m2*v2i)/(m1+m2). Final velocity of combined mass after perfectly inelastic collision. From conservation of momentum with objects sticking together. OpenStax Vol 1 Eq 9.17; Halliday Eq 9-52. CONDITION: valid only for a perfectly inelastic collision; categorical input collision_type guarded == 'perfectly_inelastic'.
